clippings.speaker: Francis Ford Coppola
clippings.quote: there's a young actor that I know. He has never been in a movie, but every time I read the scenes with Michael Corleone in the book, like him walking in Sicily with the two bodyguards and the girl, I kept seeing his face. And when I read it, that's the only one whose face I saw.
clippings.title: The Godfather Speaks
clippings.context: Coppola recalls pitching Pacino to Paramount's Robert Evans for the role of Michael.

clippings.speaker: Francis Ford Coppola
clippings.quote: I finally realized why they didn't want Pacino, why they wanted Ryan O'Neal. Bob Evans wanted a Michael who looked like him. Someone who was handsome and tall. And I wanted a Michael who was more like me, who was more ethnic.
clippings.title: The Godfather Speaks
clippings.context: Coppola on the studio's resistance to casting Pacino.

clippings.speaker: Francis Ford Coppola
clippings.quote: Yeah, we remained close and we worked together. They went on to become movie stars. But they had never been the doubters. They were just these kids I brought in and they were hoping I wasn't gonna get fired.
clippings.title: The Godfather Speaks
clippings.context: Asked about Pacino, De Niro and Brando after the film's success.

clippings.speaker: Francis Ford Coppola
clippings.quote: But they also hated my casting ideas. They hated Al Pacino for the role of Michael, and they hated Marlon Brando for the role of the godfather.
clippings.title: To Make 'The Godfather' His Way, Francis Ford Coppola Waged A Studio Battle
clippings.context: Fresh Air interview with Terry Gross, originally aired 2016 and rebroadcast in 2021.

clippings.speaker: Al Pacino
clippings.quote: At that time in my life, I didn't have a choice. Francis wanted me.
clippings.title: Al Pacino: 'The Godfather gave me a new identity that was hard to cope with'
clippings.context: Pacino, asked by Dave Itzkoff how the role of Michael came up, for the film's 50th anniversary.

clippings.speaker: Al Pacino
clippings.quote: But here's the secret: For whatever reason, he wanted me and I knew that. You could feel that. And there's nothing like that, when a director wants you. It's the best thing an actor could have, really.
clippings.title: Al Pacino: 'The Godfather gave me a new identity that was hard to cope with'
clippings.context: Pacino on his Godfather screen tests while the studio rejected Coppola's cast.

clippings.speaker: Al Pacino
clippings.quote: And there, sitting on a tombstone, is Francis Ford Coppola, weeping like a baby. Profusely crying. And I went up to him and I said, "Francis, what's wrong? What happened?" He says, "They won't give me another shot." … And I thought: OK. I guess I'm in a good film here. Because he had this kind of passion and there it is.
clippings.title: Al Pacino: 'The Godfather gave me a new identity that was hard to cope with'
clippings.context: Pacino recalls the end of shooting Vito Corleone's funeral scene.

notes: All quotes are about The Godfather; nothing found on Part II/III within budget. Irish Times reprint of a 2022 NYT Itzkoff interview (Irish Times dated 2022-03-14; exact NYT day not confirmed).
